section_summary: This section traces a dispute over Japan’s six-month oil storage requirement. American and British oil companies proposed an independent storage company, then turned to possible arrangements with Mitsui to avoid setting a precedent for their operations elsewhere. Embassy reports and company cables record Japanese officials’ responses, oil import quotas, refinery applications, and interest in producing gasoline from coal.

people.name: Stanley K. Hornbeck
people.role: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: Kurusu
people.role: Chief, Bureau of Commercial Affairs, Japanese Foreign Office

people.name: Yoshino
people.role: Japanese Vice Minister for Commerce and Industry

people.name: W. C. Teagle
people.role: Standard Oil Company of New Jersey official

people.name: Mackay
people.role: Department of State participant in oil discussion

people.name: John Lee Byrnes

subfiles.title: Corrected copy of Grew’s telegram No. 77
subfiles.about: Grew proposes seeking suspension of Japan’s oil storage regulations during negotiations with Mitsui.
subfiles.summary: Standard-Vacuum asks the Embassy to support a pause in the regulations while oil companies negotiate with Mitsui. Grew has approached Kurusu informally and plans to consult the Vice Minister alongside the British Ambassador.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 77 on American oil interests
subfiles.about: A second filed copy reports the proposed Mitsui negotiations and planned diplomatic approach.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that the oil interests are approaching Mitsui and asks whether he should urge suspension of storage regulations until negotiations finish.

subfiles.title: Department telegram No. 33 to Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department urges careful coordination before supporting the companies’ proposed Mitsui approach.
subfiles.summary: The Department approves Grew’s informal action but says the companies’ plan remains undeveloped. It advises the Embassy to confirm that negotiations are under way and coordinate discreetly with the companies and British Embassy.

subfiles.title: Parks letter enclosing Yokohama cable
subfiles.from: P. N. Parks, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Parks forwards a March 16 cable from Standard-Vacuum’s Yokohama representative.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the cable and notes that London received a similar message.

subfiles.title: Yokohama cable on storage-company proposal
subfiles.about: Local representatives report Japanese objections to an independent company carrying required oil stocks.
subfiles.summary: Kurusu and Yoshino question how a storage company would earn income and warn that foreign import quotas could be cut if the companies do not comply. Embassy representatives suggest agent financing and a fee for access to stored oil. The cable also discusses possible refinery expansion and coal-derived gasoline.

subfiles.title: Parks letter enclosing March 19 cables
subfiles.from: P. N. Parks, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Parks supplies cables sent to Yokohama by the American and British oil interests.
subfiles.summary: Encloses two telegrams and proposes discussing them with Hornbeck.

subfiles.title: Instructions to explore an arrangement with Mitsui
subfiles.from: Standard-Vacuum and British oil interests, New York and London
subfiles.about: The companies propose exploring a Mitsui arrangement while seeking a pause in storage regulations.
subfiles.summary: The head offices reject a dealers’ association and favor approaching Mitsui, with later negotiations in New York. They leave the order of approaches to Mitsui and Japanese officials to local representatives.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram No. 78
subfiles.about: Grew reports a favorable response to the proposed use of Japanese capital.
subfiles.summary: Yoshino promises unchanged quotas for the next quarter and continued delay of refinery applications. Grew and his British colleague decide to reserve formal representations for a later need.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of oil-conversation memoranda
subfiles.about: The Department sends memoranda of March 19 and March 23 conversations with oil officials.
subfiles.summary: Transmits two conversation memoranda for the Ambassador’s information.

subfiles.title: Division note on despatch No. 1723
subfiles.about: A file note assesses an earlier Embassy report on oil negotiations and coal hydrogenation.
subfiles.summary: Finds the despatch overtaken by later news; flags negotiations over a coal-hydrogenation process.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1723: American oil interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Embassy reviews February negotiations over oil storage and reports talks on coal liquefaction.
subfiles.summary: Japanese officials suggest a fixed ceiling on required stocks, compensation, and guarantees of future business. The companies consider a plan for Japanese government ownership of extra stocks, but local representatives doubt it would be acceptable. Grew also reports technical discussions over a coal liquefaction process and Mitsui’s interest in a competing process.

subfiles.title: Dickover–Kurusu conversation
subfiles.about: Kurusu conveys Yoshino’s proposed terms for continued oil negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Yoshino insists the six-month rule remains but invites a proposal for a fixed stock ceiling, compensation, and future trade guarantees. He links progress to continued quotas and postponement of domestic refinery approvals.

subfiles.title: Yokohama cable relaying Yoshino’s proposal
subfiles.about: Local representatives relay Japanese terms and recommend a concrete counterproposal.
subfiles.summary: The cable describes Yoshino’s proposed stock ceiling, compensation, and guarantees, together with warnings about quotas and refinery approvals. Local representatives recommend prompt negotiations.

subfiles.title: London cable proposing government-owned storage
subfiles.about: London suggests that Japan finance and own the extra stocks and tanks.
subfiles.summary: Proposes government-owned storage that companies could acquire as trade grows; instructs local representatives to seek views without presenting the idea to Japan.

subfiles.title: Yokohama reply on government-owned storage
subfiles.about: Local representatives explain why complete Japanese government financing seems impractical.
subfiles.summary: Warns that the proposal could cost Japan prestige, prompt more refining, and require comparable financing for domestic companies.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck telephone memorandum
subfiles.about: Parker asks about instructing Grew to seek suspension of storage requirements.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck declines to promise a specific instruction, then telephones Parker with the substance of Grew’s latest report.

subfiles.title: March 19 conversation with oil company officials
subfiles.about: Teagle and Parker discuss a possible arrangement with Mitsui with Department officials.
subfiles.summary: The companies consider a joint approach to Mitsui and hope Japan will suspend the storage regulations during negotiations. Hornbeck sees no objection to exploring the plan; no Department action is requested.

subfiles.title: Division note on Standard-Vacuum’s March 24 cable
subfiles.about: The note highlights possible Japanese partners and proposed fuel legislation.
subfiles.summary: Flags consortium possibilities, proposed fuel laws, and a reported gasoline tax.

subfiles.title: Parker letter enclosing March 24 cable
subfiles.about: Parker forwards the latest Yokohama report and awaits Mitsui’s response.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the cable and says the company awaits word from Mitsui.

subfiles.title: March 24 Yokohama cable
subfiles.about: The cable reports Japanese officials’ favorable reception of talks involving Japanese capital.
subfiles.summary: Yoshino offers unchanged quotas and delay of refinery approvals, while indicating that a consortium or separate Japanese partners might be preferable to Mitsui alone. The cable notes proposed fuel legislation.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck acknowledgment to Parker
subfiles.about: Hornbeck acknowledges Parker’s March 24 letter and cable.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Parker for details supplementing the Embassy’s telegram.

subfiles.title: Copy of Parker letter
subfiles.about: A second filed copy forwards the Yokohama cable and notes that Mitsui’s answer is pending.
subfiles.summary: Duplicates Parker’s letter forwarding the March 24 cable.

subfiles.title: Clear copy of March 24 Yokohama cable
subfiles.about: The cable details Yoshino’s assurances and possible Japanese partners.
subfiles.summary: Reports unchanged April–June quotas, delayed refinery approvals, possible arrangements with Japanese interests, and proposed fuel laws and a gasoline tax.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to oil-monopoly report
subfiles.about: The note points to another file on foreign oil interests’ negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references a report on the status of oil negotiations.

subfiles.title: Extract on January oil negotiations
subfiles.about: An extract recounts improving prospects for agreement during January.
subfiles.summary: Japanese officials appeared increasingly willing to offer concessions after recognizing the companies would not accept uncompensated six-month stocks.

subfiles.title: Division note on despatch No. 1747
subfiles.about: The note assesses the Embassy’s March 20 account of oil negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Expects further reports on a possible joint enterprise with Mitsui.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1747: American oil interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew reviews efforts to form a storage company and reports Japanese coal-fuel developments.
subfiles.summary: The foreign companies propose an independently financed storage company, but Japanese officials question its legality and funding. Embassy officers suggest fees and financing by Japanese agents to keep talks alive. Grew also reports estimates suggesting coal-derived gasoline could compete with imported fuel and a report that Mitsui bought a German process.

subfiles.title: Notes on March 11 Foreign Office meeting
subfiles.about: Ely and Meyer present the storage-company proposal to Kurusu and Yoshino.
subfiles.summary: The companies propose a fixed stock ceiling, business guarantees, and independent financing to avoid an international precedent. Yoshino warns that quotas may be cut and domestic refinery permits granted if the companies do not comply. The discussion also covers possible withdrawal, fuel substitutes, and the companies’ concerns about quotas in Korea.

subfiles.title: March 13 Dickover–Macrae–Kurusu conversation
subfiles.about: Embassy officers discuss obstacles to financing an independent storage company.
subfiles.summary: Kurusu says government, company, and private financing each pose difficulties. Dickover raises a fee for access to stored oil and possible investment by Japanese agents; Kurusu agrees to seek Yoshino’s view.

subfiles.title: Outline of proposed storage company
subfiles.about: The companies set out proposed stock limits, business guarantees, and independent financing.
subfiles.summary: Proposes an independent storage company funded through banks or public money while regulations remain suspended for discussion.

subfiles.title: March 16 Yokohama cable, enclosure copy
subfiles.about: The cable summarizes Japanese reactions and proposes continued development of the storage-company plan.
subfiles.summary: Kurusu and Yoshino question the plan and warn of quota cuts, fines, and refinery expansion. Embassy representatives suggest Japanese-agent financing and a small company fee. The cable also considers state control and coal hydrogenation.

subfiles.title: Transmittal concerning despatch No. 1747
subfiles.about: The Department forwards correspondence and memoranda concerning the oil situation.
subfiles.summary: Transmits related correspondence and memoranda; the OCR obscures their precise list.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Byrnes oil-company proposal
subfiles.about: The note points to John Lee Byrnes’s proposal for a company supplying oil to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Byrnes’s proposed oil production and refining company.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Mexican petroleum report
subfiles.about: The note points to remarks on Japan’s interest in Mexican petroleum.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references a report on Japanese interest in Mexican oil.

subfiles.title: Division note on despatch No. 1757
subfiles.about: The note summarizes a shift toward possible arrangements with Mitsui.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the companies are considering Mitsui arrangements and that both ambassadors are withholding representations.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1757: American oil interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew reports the companies’ shift from an independent storage company toward a Mitsui arrangement.
subfiles.summary: The companies explore a contractual relationship with Mitsui while preserving their separate identities. Kurusu and Yoshino respond favorably; Yoshino promises unchanged quotas and delayed refinery approvals but gives no formal assurance beyond July 1. Mitsui directors express interest and prefer negotiations in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: March 19 New York cable to Yokohama
subfiles.from: Standard-Vacuum and British oil interests, New York
subfiles.about: The head offices direct representatives to explore a Mitsui arrangement.
subfiles.summary: Rejects a dealers’ association, favors Mitsui, and seeks later negotiations in New York while the regulations remain suspended.

subfiles.title: Notes on March 23 Foreign Office conversation
subfiles.about: Ely and Meyer explain the proposed Mitsui approach to Kurusu and Yoshino.
subfiles.summary: Yoshino discusses Mitsui’s oil-import position; the conversation continues beyond this section.
